subject: Onboarding: model shortlist, context lanes & token bands (Clearsight)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ella Park <ella@clearsight.ai>, Jake Morris <jake@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: model shortlist, context lanes & token bands

Hi Ella / Jake — great to meet you last week. Moving the onboarding plan into execution: attached is our first-pass token-band worksheet and a brief model-shortlist sketch. Goal for this message: confirm the traffic assumptions and context length needs so Marcus can lock a recommended serving lane.

Quick summary of what I need from you this week:
- Confirm which product flows will be live in MVP (chat assistant, batch summaries, and search re-rank) and estimated requests/day for each. I put our guesses in the attached spreadsheet.
- For chat flows, confirm max context you want preserved (conversation depth) — I put options 2k / 8k / 32k in the sheet.
- Any regulatory constraints around data retention or private hosting? (we flagged VPC in the notes if needed)

Attachments: [clearsight_token_estimates_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)], [model_shortlist_notes_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]

High-level model shortlist (working):
- redwood/clarity-13b (quantized) — balanced latency/cost, good for long context with prefix caching
- open/mistral-7b-instruct — lower-cost lane for high-volume classification and short-text summaries
- falcon-40b-instruct (8-bit) — high-quality NLU where hallucination sensitivity is highest

Marcus, Lauren, looping you for technical and prompt/embedding considerations. Ella/Jake, any corrections to the traffic numbers will change model lane recommendations and cost banding.

Thanks — Priyom
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ella Park <ella@clearsight.ai>

Cc: Jake Morris <jake@clearsight.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearsight.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jan 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist, context lanes & token bands

Thanks Priyom — we reviewed the attachment and added comments in the token sheet (column note: product_flow_comments). A few clarifications:
- MVP flows: chat assistant (conversational support for web + mobile), automated weekly summary (batch), and on-demand legal-doc search (re-rank).
- Estimated traffic: chat 12k req/day, summaries 600 jobs/day (avg 4k tokens/job), search re-rank 3k req/day.
- For chat, we need conversation depth to 8k tokens (customers frequently paste long transcripts).
- We prefer hosted but will evaluate Private for legal-docs if redaction is required.

Question for Marcus: for the 8k conversation lane, what's a realistic P99 latency target if we pick the clarity-13b quantized lane vs the 40b lane? Also any guidance on caching prefixes for repeated system prompts?

-Ella
Head of Product
Clearsight

Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist, context lanes & token bands

Priyom / team — read through the notes and Ella's clarifications. Quick technical take and recommended lanes:

1) Latency expectations (P99) for chat (8k context)
- redwood/clarity-13b (int8/8-bit quantized): ~420-700 ms P99 for streaming top-k on an A100-like node with prefix caching enabled and batching window tuned to 20-40ms.
- falcon-40b-instruct (8-bit): ~1.1-1.6s P99 under similar batching; better semantic fidelity for edge cases but higher cost and memory pressure.

2) Cache strategy
- System prompts and common instruction prefixes: keep in KV cache per conversation id; this reduces repeated compute for first N tokens. Clearsight's long transcript pattern makes prefix caching valuable.
- For summaries, we recommend batch-mode (no streaming) with a larger batching window to maximize throughput.

3) Token-band and throughput mapping (very rough)
- Chat (12k req/day, median 1.2k tokens per session): clarity-13b lane -> ~15M tokens/day; mistral-7b lane for lightweight intents -> ~6M tokens/day; reserve a 40b fallback for 5% of calls (high-fidelity).

4) Recommendations and immediate asks
- Confirm whether legal-doc search requires Private deployment (we assume hosted for now). If Private required, Marcus to run a quick capacity sketch for on-prem hosting (will need sample doc sizes).
- Priyom / Lauren: I'll sketch a concrete lane mapping (primary/secondary/fallback) and send a short ops playbook with autoscale knobs.

Attachment: [model_shortlist_notes_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]

--Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
